statement: The full arbitrary-germ characterization is not obtained; exact point-germ, residual, stability and surjective-tower cases are proved separately.
notes: The unrestricted replacement assertion in Lead 14 is refuted by F.8.

statement: For a small cofiltered coherent system with coherent transition morphisms, finite locally constant objects descend; the characteristic-zero strict henselian normal-crossings étale limit and its finite fundamental group are identified.
answers: Task F.2; Lead 21 scheme assertions; Lead 21 scheme-limit; Lead 21 scheme-finite; Lead 21 scheme-classifying
notes: All finite trivializing data and their finite covering condition are descended explicitly. Local dimension one gives a classifying topos; higher dimension does not. Lead 21 scheme-limit: The strict henselian normal-crossings punctured scheme has the inverse-limit étale topos. Regular strict henselian local ring in characteristic zero. Lead 21 scheme-finite: Its finite coverings are finite continuous Zhat(1)^r-sets. r is the number of geometric branches. Lead 21 scheme-classifying: At a point on the divisor, the limit is a classifying topos exactly in local dimension one. Dimension greater than one supplies a proper nonempty open subterminal.

statement: The two manuscript readings are decided in the proved subclasses, but a characterization for every germ remains open.
notes: Leroy supplies the locally Galois replacement and precise groupoid-limit results; he does not assert the false unrestricted comparison.

statement: The complex normal-crossings homotopy limit is the tangent torus; a rational cusp over a number field gives a completed-Kummer torsor of homotopy fixed points with trivial fundamental groups.
depends_on: Stix Theorem 14, supplied version; Kummer theory and finite Mittag-Leffler systems
notes: Rational tangent vectors inject densely and properly. Packet injection uses proper-point injectivity over finite extensions. Lead 17(a): The complex normal-crossings punctured homotopy limit is the tangent torus, despite an empty strict intersection. Coordinate polydisc cofinality is stated. Lead 17(b): The number-field rational-cusp homotopy fixed points form the completed Kummer torsor, with no lim1 term, trivial pi1, and dense proper rational tangent subset. Point/cusp packet injectivity hypotheses are checked.

statement: The literal disjunction in the proposed homotopy reformulation is automatic for the hyperbolic K(pi,1); the non-tautological cuspidal section conjecture remains a surjectivity problem.
notes: Automaticity is proved, but alone does not refute logical equivalence with a conjecture that may itself be true. Identifying all curve homotopy fixed points with rational points is false in the presence of a rational cusp.

statement: The unrestricted étale-stack torus and geometric-fibre assertions in Lead 21 are false.
depends_on: Explicit stack BC2 times a disk; fgh_topology_checks.py
answers: Task F.6; Lead 21(B,C), unrestricted stacks; Lead 21 B-stack; Lead 21 C-stack
notes: The punctured germ retains BC2, so H1 is Z plus Z/2. The same counterexample has an effective bidisc quotient realization. Intrinsic residual-gerbe and geometric point fibres differ. Lead 21 B-stack: The unrestricted identification with a geometric point fibre is false; the intrinsic residual-gerbe version is true for closed nested stages. BC2 times a disk distinguishes the fibres. Lead 21 C-stack: The unrestricted torus-homology formula is false for stacks with isotropy. The actual homotopy fibre retains BC2 and H1 torsion.

statement: The inverse limit of open-subspace sheaf topoi is the sheaf topos of the intersection sublocale; for a closed subset of a regular Hausdorff space the ordinary germ is the closed subset and the residual germ is empty.
answers: Task F.1; Task F.3; Lead 14, localic assertions

statement: There are locally connected, semilocally simply connected covering germs which cannot be the locally constant objects of any Grothendieck topos.
depends_on: Discrete tails of N and diagonal argument
answers: Task F.1; Task F.3; Lead 14, replacement assertion
notes: The covering-germ category lacks a countable coproduct of its terminal object. Representatives are chosen simultaneously after filling their individually finite undefined prefixes. Lead 14: The localic intersection and Hausdorff point/residual assertions are true, but the unrestricted classifying-topos replacement assertion is false. Discrete tails have no countable terminal coproduct.

statement: Normal-crossings covering germs are Z^r-sets; nested closed blow-up stages have the closed fibre as limit, and tubular neighbourhood germs of closed submanifolds have the expected coverings.
answers: Task F.1; Task F.2; Task F.3; Lead 21(B), manifolds; Lead 21 B-manifold
notes: The arbitrary Z^r-action category differs from the finite continuous profinite-action category. Lead 21 B-manifold: Nested closed compact blow-up stages have the blow-up fibre as their sheaf-topos limit. Stages must be closed in one fixed ambient blow-up; merely saying compact in a non-Hausdorff setting is insufficient.

statement: For a countable surjective tower of discrete groups, the inverse limit of classifying topoi is the classifying topos of the prodiscrete limit and its locally constant objects are the stagewise colimit.
answers: Task F.1; Task F.3; Lead 14, corrected replacement
notes: All continuous actions need not be locally constant: the disjoint union of Z/2^n is a counterexample for Z2.

statement: Compactness of a closed subset alone does not give full faithfulness for arbitrary covering descent.
depends_on: Cantor subset of R and the family of digit functions
notes: Every finite family of digit functions descends; the countable family does not descend to one neighbourhood.

statement: For a decreasing coordinate neighbourhood basis at a complex normal-crossings point, the strict singular-chain limit is zero and the degreewise lim1 complex recovers torus homology with the stated shift.
depends_on: Roos complex and Milnor exact sequence
answers: Task F.6; Lead 21(C), manifolds; Lead 21 C-manifold
notes: For stacks the torus must be replaced by the actual isotropy-retaining homotopy fibre. Lead 21 C-manifold: The zero strict chain limit and shifted lim1 torus-homology identities hold. A decreasing basis at a normal-crossings point is used.

statement: Leroy proves the locally Galois sum-completion theorem, precise classifying-topos limits and a van Kampen theorem, with hypotheses distinct from arbitrary covering-germ descent.
notes: Original scan and provisional transcription were read together; no theorem is inferred from the title alone.

statement: Under connected classical covering hypotheses and surjective maps from the limit fundamental group, arbitrary covering descent is equivalent to eventual fundamental-group stability.
notes: The surjectivity and connected, locally path connected, semilocally simply connected hypotheses are explicit.

statement: A countable intersection of open subspaces of a locally compact Hausdorff space is spatial as a sublocale intersection, with its subspace topology.
answers: Task F.6; Lead 21(A), manifolds; Lead 21 A-manifold
notes: The intersection K need not be closed or compact; the ambient local compactness and countability are used. Lead 21 A-manifold: The countable open-neighbourhood inverse limit is Sh(K minus Z). Locally compact Hausdorff manifold; K need not be closed.

statement: The intrinsic étale-stack version of the countable-open intersection theorem holds with a locally compact Hausdorff atlas; nested closed substacks have the expected intrinsic intersection limit.
answers: Task F.6; Lead 21(A,B), corrected stacks; Lead 21 A-stack
notes: Neighbourhoods must be intrinsic open substacks; a residual-gerbe fibre also needs a downstairs family actually shrinking to that gerbe. A locally compact Hausdorff atlas alone does not guarantee a Hausdorff orbit space. The geometric point 2-fibre differs. Lead 21 A-stack: The intrinsic open-substack version holds for an étale stack with locally compact Hausdorff atlas. Chartwise neighbourhood choices not defining open substacks are excluded.

statement: For every Hausdorff point germ, arbitrary covering descent and existence of any locally-constant-topos realization are equivalent to every neighbourhood quasi-component being a neighbourhood.
notes: The convergent sequence at its limit point gives an explicit failure. This is an exact characterization for all Hausdorff point germs.

statement: For a closed subset Y of a regular Hausdorff space, the residual covering germ agrees with its literal limit exactly when Y is open.
depends_on: F.7 and persistence of empty versus terminal covers
notes: This is an exact residual closed-subset criterion.

statement: For every compact subset of a locally compact Hausdorff space, finite coverings and their morphisms descend to one open neighbourhood, without local connectivity assumptions.
depends_on: Finite frame-bundle join construction; neighbourhood retraction; properness of finite covers
answers: Task F.1; Task F.2; Task F.3
notes: The ordinary finite-cover comparison is an equivalence for the Cantor germ, while arbitrary-cover full faithfulness fails.

statement: The actual arithmetic scalar lambda and its asserted rationality are not determined.
notes: G.9 proves lambda−31/20 is integral, v5(lambda)=−1 and 5lambda=4 mod5. The scalar 31/20+sqrt(6) satisfies this congruence and the universal constraints; it is not an arithmetic Galois counterexample. Lead 15: Rationality of the actual degree-eight arithmetic scalar remains unproved and unrefuted.

statement: The actual alpha-image is Z5 and the image is saturated in its rational line; the second coordinate of its normalized generator remains unknown.
notes: G.9 gives image Z5(C8+delta B8) with delta=lambda−31/20 integral and saturation index1. An actual eighth-Johnson element has alpha=1, nu=delta, but delta has not been evaluated. The index in the full rank-two ambient lattice is infinite.

statement: The embedded arithmetic generators and integral lattices in all repeated-character spaces of degrees eight through fourteen are not determined.
notes: Ambient dimensions and metabelian characters do not specify these embeddings.

statement: The degree-eight ambient vectors, word coordinates, metabelian projection, and saturated Z5 lattice are independently certified.
answers: Task G.1; Task G.2; Task G.3
notes: C8=A8+(31/20)B8 and B8 form the saturated integral basis; alpha,nu are the dual integral coordinates.

statement: Every 5-adic scalar gives an allowed universal geometric degree-eight direction; these constraints do not force rationality.
depends_on: Enriquez Proposition 4.19 and inclusion after (49); G.4
notes: The Hensel root sqrt(6) in Q5 is an explicit irrational allowed scalar, not an arithmetic Galois counterexample.

statement: For delta=lambda-31/20, m=max(0,-v5(delta)), and alpha-image 5^a Z5, the arithmetic index in its saturated line is exactly 5^(a-m).
notes: G.9 now proves a=m=0 for the actual Galois action; delta remains unknown.

statement: A degree-nine finite Magnus quotient measures alpha and nu of an actual eighth-Johnson automorphism without logarithmic division.
depends_on: Truncated noncommutative power series over Z/5^r
notes: The recipe is finite and explicit; an actual arithmetic automorphism remains to be supplied and evaluated.

statement: Malkin’s cited depth-two Hodge results do not provide the unconditional motivic-to-5-adic comparison required by Lead15.
depends_on: Malkin Theorems11,16 and conditional discussion before Lemma3
notes: The primary source explicitly conditions the realization transfer on motivic formalism and regulator injectivity.

statement: The exact conductor-four Soulé image on Delta and its eighth Johnson subgroup is 5Z5; the actual alpha-image is Z5 and its arithmetic line is saturated, with lambda−31/20 integral.
where_proved: sections/G.tex; code/fgh_primitive_degree8.py, JSON and stdout; code/de_soule_conductor4.py
depends_on: G.4,G.6; Ishii–Goto Definition2.14, Remark2.15(2), Theorem1.7; Nakamura1995 Sections4.3–4.9, Corollary4.12; Nakamura2013 p492 erratum; Ishii2026 Theorem1.2,Lemma1.5; Hain–Matsumoto Proposition20.1,Corollary20.2,Section22
answers: Task G.1; Task G.2; Task G.3
notes: Exact q101 certificate u1=97 and u1^20=36 proves primitivity off the cyclotomic line. Integral group filters kill all lower Johnson characters with unit multipliers. The actual prefactor d^3/267840 is independently checked, including factor12 and the metabelian sign. Thus v5(lambda)=−1, 5lambda=4 mod5, and saturation index1; the nonmetabelian value nu is still unevaluated.

statement: The images of the five retained normalizer/conjugator sources on every higher relative stage are not determined.
notes: Ambient scheme automorphisms are not identified with the actual profinite source images.

statement: The individual kernels for the five retained sources at every stage are not determined.
notes: A general affine action criterion and the joint full-prime abelian-stage kernel are proved separately.

statement: Extension of every additive-polynomial first-stage lift to the unspecified integral nonabelian tower remains open.
notes: All abelian Fermat stages admit the same lift. A specific class-two quotient obstructs it, but its canonical integral comparison at 2 is not established.

statement: The first integral q2 model and its dual-number idempotence obstruction have been rerun and verified.
answers: Task H.1; Task H.2; Task H.3
notes: 110592 cocycle identities and 2304 projection identities checked; epsilon is not idempotent and the corresponding minimal automorphism does not lift.

statement: Every additive-polynomial automorphism f over an F2-algebra with f(1)=1 acts compatibly on every abelian Fermat stage.
depends_on: Integral cocycle and matrix formulas; code/fgh_additive_lifts.py
notes: The polynomial T+epsilon(T^2-T) is detected on F4[epsilon], not on F2[epsilon]-points.

statement: A coordinatewise additive automorphism on a Heisenberg abelianization extends to a group automorphism only if it is multiplicative; the displayed nonlinear example fails.
notes: This is a complete counterexample for the stated Heisenberg model. It is not asserted to settle the canonical Fermat nonabelian model at 2.

statement: Actual profinite actions on each integral abelian stage are affine linear with a precise identity criterion, and the joint full-prime abelian-stage kernel is the kernel on the full metabelian quotient.
depends_on: Intersection of closed commutators of K_n equals F second derived group
notes: The criterion is genuine-action and choice-dependent; it is not an unqualified outer-action assertion.

statement: The nonlinear additive-polynomial direction is outside the actual profinite signed-action image on the integral abelian stages.
notes: Ambient group-scheme kernel directions and retained profinite source images are different objects.

statement: The rank-five naive Hall class-two group scheme cannot carry the verified modular rho action after reduction modulo2.
notes: rho sends e2 to e1+e4; their squares are incompatible, for every central lift.

statement: The same rational class-two group and designated abelian quotient admit integral models with opposite nonlinear-lift behaviour at2.
notes: The laws with central terms ab-prime and 2ab-prime are rationally isomorphic; their characteristic-two fibres differ.
